comparator.name: Bachelor Automotive Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: The official after-revision EE/AT curriculum for 2026–2027, latest version 2 July 2026, was freshly retrieved and visually inspected on 8 October 2026. Only common and AT rows form this Automotive Technology reconstruction; EE-only rows are alternatives and are not stacked into the degree. Current core totals 125 EC, including 5XEC0 Final Bachelor Project 10, with ITEC Ethics 0LVX30 5 and ITEC Society 0LVX40 5 (10 total) and genuine free elective space 45. This replaces the older 120-core/15-USE-ITEC/45 allocation. Year one is 60 core EC; year two is 40 core + 5 ITEC + 15 free; year three is 25 core including project + 5 ITEC + 30 free. All 27 course/project/open-space positions total 180. Current 4AUB10 is Propulsion Systems, and is not relabelled as the older Electric and Hybrid Propulsion Systems. DBL Autonomous Vehicles Conquering the World 5AID0, DBL Automotive Design Project Electronic Differential 5XSC0 and Semiconductor Technology 5XPG0 appear among optional courses, not universal compulsory core; they are not added as required formation. Open electives retain university approval, overlap and applicable level conditions; no example optional course is forced into the free space. The curriculum table establishes required membership and credits, not a guarantee of exact future timetable or individual course admission. The project row uses ambiguous quarter/timeslot notation; no exact scheduling claim is inferred from it.

alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical system models with programming, algorithms, computer vision, robotics, machine learning, networks, product design and lifecycle assessment to study sensing, autonomous decisions and connected mobility. This is a computational systems response, not a vehicle-engineering substitute.

alternatives.concept: Retain mathematical modelling, perception, robotics and intelligent decisions while adding lifecycle assessment, renewable-energy design, climate context and material recovery for lower-impact mobility and product systems.

alternatives.labelRationale: Five sustainability courses provide a cumulative lifecycle, energy and resource strand alongside quantitative intelligent-system methods; the label does not imply battery, power-electronics or vehicle-design engineering.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ: discrete logic, databases, networks, advanced algorithms and AI ethics are replaced by two sustainability foundations, climate change, renewable-system design and resource recovery. These changes implement the evidenced low-impact electric-mobility direction.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Programming precedes algorithms, networks, planning and reinforcement learning; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Numerical Methods and Linear Systems occur in the sole available fourth semester, while Advanced Calculus follows when next offered.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two related-fields responses pass the academic and mechanical gates and differ by five courses / 37.5 EC. A further vehicle-mechanics and propulsion direction cannot supply mechanics, thermodynamics, road-vehicle dynamics, circuits, electromagnetics, electromechanics, power electronics or powertrain laboratories. General calculus, linear systems, robotics and renewable-energy assessment cannot be relabelled as that physical-engineering formation. The 45 EC of genuine external free choice remains open and is not used to manufacture another target route.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both directly teach calculus used to formulate quantitative systems; UCR also covers broader mathematical methods.
Both directly address signals and linear-system representations; UCR does not reproduce the surrounding electrical-engineering laboratories.
The generic Math 1 title does not establish a more specific content match beyond the separately aligned calculus component.
The generic Math 2 title does not establish a sufficiently specific course-level counterpart.
Both include programming and computational problem solving; the 10-EC external component also contains an engineering challenge that UCR programming does not reproduce.
Both address sensing-informed computation and action; UCR Robotics is computational and does not reproduce embedded automotive sensing/actuation hardware.
Both address communication networks; UCR covers general internet and operating systems rather than in-vehicle protocols and hardware.
Both examine ethical issues in technology; UCR focuses specifically on AI ethics and is not the complete external ITEC unit.
Both use multidisciplinary team design and development; UCR concerns general consumer products rather than an automotive engineering integration project.

UCR has no thermodynamics and automotive propulsion-systems sequence.
General programming and operating systems do not replace computer-architecture hardware.
UCR has no electromagnetics course.
Linear Systems is relevant mathematical preparation but does not reproduce the complete engineering control-systems course.
The genuine 15-EC free-elective space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.

notes.text: Automotive Technology integrates mechanics, electronics, electromechanics, power conversion, embedded hardware, vehicle networks, propulsion, road-vehicle dynamics, laboratories and an automotive final project. The UCR curricula support computational autonomous systems or sustainable energy/product systems related to mobility; they do not reproduce that complete vehicle-engineering formation.
